newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sth Australia sees A$1 mln underlying surplus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sth Australia sees A$1 mln underlying surplus.

text.p: The state of South Australia is expected to produce a balanced budget in 1997/98 (July/June) with an underlying surplus of about A$1.0 million, treasurer Stephen Baker said on Thursday.
Baker said South Australia was forecast to end 1996/97 on track with a net underlying deficit of A$59 million, with a "modest but stable and sustainable" surplus projected out to the year 2000/1.
"From today the state pays its way," Baker told parliament.

The budget papers showed the headline figure for the total public sector was estimated to be a A$258 million surplus in 1996/97, with asset sales of about A$200 million. The headline surplus was projected to fall to A$27 million in 1997/98.
No major asset sales were forecast for 1997/98.
The papers showed public sector net debt was expected to drop to around A$7.5 billion at June 30 this year from A$8.4 billion three years previously.
The ratio of debt-to-gross state product was set to decline to 19.5 percent by June 1998 from 26.4 percent in 1994.

Baker said an A$145 million job creation initiative, designed to help kick start the state's economy, had been funded by better-than-expected returns on former State Bank of South Australia assets and a compensation dividend for the Electricity Trust of South Australia.
He said South Australian gross state product was expected to have risen 2.25 percent in 1996/97 and to rise 3.0 percent in 1997/98, below the national average of 3.75 percent.
Employment was expected to rise 1.5 percent, triple this year's rate, with a marginal impact on unemployment, Baker said.
